name: Prefrontal cortex
summary: The large anterior part of the frontal lobe in front of the premotor areas, comprising dorsolateral, orbitofrontal (ventral) and medial regions. It is the seat of executive function: planning, working memory, cognitive flexibility, judgement, inhibition of inappropriate responses, and the motivation and social calibration of behavior. Its three regions fail in three recognizable ways: the dorsolateral patient cannot plan or shift, the orbitofrontal patient is disinhibited and tactless, and the medial patient is apathetic and mute.

anatomy.location: Frontal pole, superior and middle frontal gyri anterior to the premotor cortex, the orbital surface above the orbital roofs, and the medial surface in front of the cingulate gyrus.

subdivisions.name: Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex
subdivisions.note: working memory, planning, set shifting; connected with the mediodorsal thalamus and dorsal striatum

subdivisions.name: Orbitofrontal cortex
subdivisions.note: reward valuation, impulse control, social behavior; connected with the amygdala and olfactory cortex

function: Executive control of thought and action, working memory, emotional and social regulation, and personality.

bestView.label: middle frontal gyrus and frontal pole
orbitofrontal cortex over the orbital roof

imaging.normalAppearance: The frontal poles and orbital surfaces are prone to susceptibility artifact near the sinuses on MRI and to contusion in trauma; disproportionate frontal atrophy points to frontotemporal dementia.

pathology.finding: Frontal and anterior temporal atrophy, often asymmetric, with hypometabolism on FDG-PET.
Hemorrhagic contusions of the gyri recti and orbital gyri after a fall on the occiput (contrecoup).
Glioblastoma crossing the genu of the corpus callosum to involve both frontal lobes.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: MRI with T1 and FLAIR; FDG-PET for dementia

lesionEffects.deficit: Executive dysfunction: poor planning, perseveration, impaired set shifting

lesionEffects.mechanism: Medial prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex
Loss of prefrontal inhibition over parietal-driven actions

examination: Frontal assessment battery: fluency, similarities, Luria sequence, conflicting instructions, go/no-go, grasp
Observe for utilization and imitation behavior
pearls: Bedside cognition can be normal in devastating orbitofrontal disease; ask the family
Bilateral medial frontal lesions produce a patient who is awake but does not speak or move (akinetic mutism)
